### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 are not observed at all (0 of 200 traces); in the later window each of them appears in about 17–23 in 100 traces (34–46 of 200), at most once per trace, just past the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.51). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]
- The five behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: any pair of them shares a trace in at most about 1 in 100 later traces (several pairs never), and their shares sum to about all later traces, so nearly every later trace runs exactly one of the five. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL007, REL008, REL012, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, LAG002]
- In the earlier window, A29 passes on almost exclusively to A30 (about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) and A30 almost exclusively to A31 (about 96 in 100); in the later window A29 sends about 51 in 100 of its transitions to the five new activities and about 48 in 100 directly to A30, while A30 sends about 47 in 100 to the new activities and about 51 in 100 to A31. [DIR006, DIR007]
- Each new activity leads back into the main sequence: roughly half of its outgoing transitions go to A30 and roughly half to A31, with about 2–3 in 100 going to other activities. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Ordering: A19, A20 and A25 execute after A29 in about 21–23 in 100 traces with the reverse essentially never observed, and they precede A31 in about 20–23 in 100 traces; relative to A30, both orders occur in similar proportions (for example A19 before A30 in about 12 in 100 traces and after A30 in about 11 in 100). The incoming edges from A29 and outgoing edges to A30/A31 indicate the same placement for A26 and A27. [REL004, REL009, REL013, REL006, REL011, REL015, REL005, REL010, REL014, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Step distances shift accordingly: A29→A30, previously immediate in about 98 in 100 cases, is immediate in about 47 and two steps apart in about 50; A30→A31 moves from immediate in about 97 to immediate in about 51 and two steps in about 46; A29→A31 moves from two steps (about 95 in 100) to three steps (about 94 in 100); A31's mean relative position moves slightly later (about 0.54 to 0.56). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a five-way exclusive choice — A19, A20, A25, A26 or A27, one per trace — is inserted into the segment between A29 and A31: each of the five runs in about 17–23 in 100 later traces after being unobserved in the earlier window, always after A29 and before A31, positioned either directly between A29 and A30 or between A30 and A31 in roughly equal shares, whereas earlier A29, A30 and A31 followed one another directly. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL004, REL006, REL009, REL011, REL013, REL015, REL005, REL010, REL014, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Supporting signs: occurrence, routing, order and distance indicators all show the same picture — A29 and A30 redirect about half of their outgoing transitions to the new activities, the new activities return to A30 or A31, the one-step increase in the A29–A31 distance in about 94 in 100 later traces matches a single insertion per trace, and the five rarely co-occur; with 35 evidence items qualified against roughly 0.6 expected for an unchanged process, the volume of findings itself exceeds what random re-splits of a stable process produce. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: the comparison cannot rule out that the two windows draw different mixes of coexisting process variants rather than reflecting one process that changed; placement is also established in event-order positions, not clock time. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG002]

Other differences: beyond a few percent of the new activities' transitions leading to activities other than A30 and A31 (for example A46 after A19, A21 after A26, A03 after A27) and sub-1-in-100 fluctuations in the remaining outgoing shares of A29 and A30, no further differences appear at the configured thresholds. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 121 units tested, 35 items qualified, 0.6 expected by chance. Control flow family: 121 tested, 35 items, 0.6 expected. So 35 items vs 0.6 expected — many times larger than chance expectation. This is a strong signal that something changed (the count of qualifying items cannot be explained by chance as a whole).

Evidence items (35 total? Let me count): OCC001-005 (5), DIR001-007 (7), POS001-005 (5), REL001-015 (15), LAG001-003 (3). Total = 5+7+5+15+3 = 35. Yes, 35 items.

All empirical_strength = 0.995 (i.e., 199/200 reference comparisons had smaller differences).

Now the behaviour:

OCC items: A19, A20, A25, A26, A27 all had 0 participation before, and after: A19 23%, A20 21%, A25 23%, A26 17%, A27 17.5%. So these five activities were absent in the earlier window and appear in roughly 17–23% of traces in the later window. Recurrence support 0 in both — so they occur at most once per trace (no repeats).

DIR items: DIR001-005 for A19, A20, A25, A26, A27: before profile empty (activity never observed), after outgoing transitions mostly to A30 and A31 (roughly 45–59% to A30, 38–52% to A31, plus small shares to others). So the new activities are followed by A30 or A31.

DIR006: A29's outgoing transitions: before ~98% to A30; after ~47.5% to A30, with new transitions to A19 (12%), A25 (12%), A20 (9%), A26 (9.5%), A27 (8.5%), plus tiny others. So A29, which previously went almost always to A30, now branches to the new activities in about 41% of its outgoing transitions (12+12+9+9.5+8.5 = 41%).

DIR007: A30's outgoing: before ~95.5% to A31; after ~51% to A31, with new transitions to A20 (11.3%), A19 (9.9%), A25 (9.9%), A27 (8.9%), A26 (6.9%), plus small. So A30 now also branches to the new activities in about 47% of its outgoing transitions.

POS001-004: A19, A20, A25, A26 appear at mean relative position ~0.51-0.52 (middle of the trace) in the later window; absent before.

POS005: A31's position shifted slightly later: mean 0.540 → 0.561, median 0.538 → 0.567. Small shift (observed_change 0.023) but strength 0.995.

REL items:
- REL001 (A19,A20): before neither=100%; after A_only 22.5%, B_only 20.5%, neither 56.5%, cooccurrence 0.5%. So A19 and A20 rarely occur together — they are mostly alternatives (only ~0.5% co-occur).
- REL002 (A19,A25): after A_only 23%, B_only 23%, neither 54%, cooccurrence 0. Alternatives.
- REL003 (A19,A26): after A_only 23%, B_only 17%, neither 60%. Alternatives.
- REL004 (A19,A29): before B_only=100% (A29 always present, A19 never); after cooccurrence 23%, B_only 77%, B_before_A 23%. So A19 always occurs with A29 and after it (B_before_A = A29 before A19, 23%). So A19 occurs only in traces with A29, after A29.
- REL005 (A19,A30): before B_only 100%; after cooccurrence 23%, B_only 77%, A_before_B 12%, B_before_A 10.5%, interleaved 0.5%. So A19 co-occurs with A30 in 23% of traces, in mixed order (A19 before A30 in 12%, A30 before A19 in 10.5%).
- REL006 (A19,A31): after cooccurrence 23%, A_before_B 22.5% (A19 before A31), B_before_A 0.5%. So A19 occurs before A31.
- REL007 (A20,A25): after A_only 20%, B_only 22%, neither 57%, cooccurrence 1%. Alternatives.
- REL008 (A20,A26): after A_only 21%, B_only 17%, neither 62%. Alternatives.
- REL009 (A20,A29): after cooccurrence 21%, B_before_A 21%. A20 after A29.
- REL010 (A20,A30): after cooccurrence 21%, A_before_B 9.5%, B_before_A 11.5%. Mixed order.
- REL011 (A20,A31): after cooccurrence 21%, A_before_B 20.5%. A20 before A31.
- REL012 (A25,A26): after A_only 22.5%, B_only 16.5%, neither 60.5%. Alternatives.
- REL013 (A25,A29): after cooccurrence 23%, B_before_A 22.5%. A25 after A29.
- REL014 (A25,A30): after cooccurrence 23%, A_before_B 12.5%, B_before_A 10.5%. Mixed.
- REL015 (A25,A31): after cooccurrence 23%, A_before_B 23%. A25 before A31.

LAG items:
- LAG001 (A29,A30): before lag 1 in 98.5% of cases; after lag 1 in 46.8%, lag 2 in 50.2%, lag 3 in 1.7%. So the distance between A29 and A30 increased — A30 now often follows A29 two steps later instead of immediately.
- LAG002 (A29,A31): before lag 2 in 95%, lag 3 in 5%; after lag 2 in 0.5%, lag 3 in 94%, lag 4 in 5.5%. So distance shifted from 2 to 3.
- LAG003 (A30,A31): before lag 1 in 96.5%; after lag 1 in 51.5%, lag 2 in 45.8%. Distance increased.

Hmm, if the new activity is followed by A30, then new activity before A30. But mixed order suggests sometimes A30 before the new activity. And DIR007 shows A30 leading to the new activities. So possibly the new activities can be placed either between A29 and A30, or between A30 and A31. Actually, let's think: A29 → new → A30 → A31, or A29 → A30 → new → A31. And LAG: A29→A30 distance increases (because new activity inserted between them in some traces), A29→A31 distance increases from 2 to 3, A30→A31 distance increases (new activity inserted between them in some traces).

So the picture: a block of five alternative activities (A19, A20, A25, A26, A27 — one chosen per trace, mutually exclusive) inserted in the segment between A29 and A31, in roughly 17–23% of traces (about one in five). A26 17%, A27 17.5%. If overlaps are tiny (0.5-1%), total with any ≈ 23+21+23+17+17.5 − small overlaps ≈ ~99-100%? That seems too high. Hmm wait, that would mean nearly every trace has one new activity. But REL001 "neither" = 56.5% for A19,A20 — that's consistent: 43.5% have A19 or A20; the rest have A25/A26/A27 (56.5% ≈ 23+17+17.5 = 57.5, minus overlaps ≈ 56.5). Hmm wait, but that changes the interpretation: it's not that a new optional branch appears in ~20% of traces; it's that in the later window, essentially every trace executes one of five alternative activities in the middle segment, whereas in the earlier window none of them appeared. That's a major structural change: five new alternative activities inserted between A29 and A30/A31.

Hold on. Let me double check the "neither" numbers. REL001: after neither = 0.565. If A19 (23%) and A20 (21%) are disjoint except 0.5% co-occurrence, then A19-or-A20 = 43.5%, neither = 56.5%. ✓.

So in the later window, every trace has one of {A19, A20, A25, A26, A27}. And these always co-occur with A29 (REL004/009/013: cooccurrence equals participation, B_only = 77-79%, A_only = 0). So the structure: before: ... A29 → A30 → A31 ... (A29→A30 immediate in 98.5% of lag observations, A30→A31 immediate in 96.5%, A29→A31 at lag 2 in 95%). After: A29 → {one of A19/A20/A25/A26/A27} → A30 → A31, or possibly A29 → A30 → {new} → A31.

So this is an insertion of a new alternative block, not a shift in path frequencies between existing paths. The instructions note: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows... Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence is direct (REL, LAG, DIR all show the relations directly), consistent (all items agree), and the screening count is ~58× the chance expectation. Competing explanations: could this be a rare variant appearing in one window? No — the new activities appear in ~17-23% of traces each, ~100% collectively, in 200 traces; that's not a rare variant.
